style.visual_cues: Plan anticipation, impact, compression or extension, rebound, and settling. Align deformation with movement while preserving apparent volume and recognizable silhouettes. Use timing variation and short holds; avoid making every object bounce or deform continuously.
style.note: The source directly names or describes this visual direction. An animation principle rather than an independent art movement.

recommended_stack.name: chroma.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally validate colors, derive controlled palette variants, interpolate colors, and check foreground/background contrast.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Start with task-provided colors and the style visual_cues. Keep a shared, deterministic palette and named color tokens. Generate gradients or interpolate colors only when the style permits them; keep limited-palette, monochrome, pixel, and print treatments discrete where required. Evaluate animated color from shared composition time. Check contrast against the actual composited background; a two-color ratio alone does not verify text over transparency, gradients, textures, or video. Pass output through the selected renderer's color API and preserve its color-space handling. Native CSS/SVG colors remain sufficient when no color processing is needed.

Validate approved colors and assess readable existing token pairs with chroma-js. Use palette.gradient only when enabled and appropriate. Preserve task/reference colors exactly; optional suggested tokens are fallback inputs, not permission to recolor assets.

recommended_stack.name: Extended Position-Based Dynamics (XPBD)
recommended_stack.runtime: Depends on the selected solver implementation: JavaScript, WebAssembly, native offline code or a supported GPU backend
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally simulate compliant constrained motion for cloth, elastic deformable bodies and suitable physical interactions. XPBD is an algorithm, not a visual style, renderer, animation framework or package name.
recommended_stack.implementation_selection: Prefer an existing maintained solver that explicitly supports XPBD and the required constraint and collision models. Verify its actual API, licensing, runtime and determinism before use. Do not assume that a generic physics package implements XPBD, or invent a universal XPBD API. The reference examples are educational starting points, not a production dependency recommendation.
constraint_options: Distance or stretch constraints for connections and cloth structure
Bending constraints for cloth or deliberately modeled paper folds
Volume or constitutive strain constraints for the chosen elastic-body model
Attachment or prescribed-position constraints for anchors and authored controls
Contact and self-collision handling appropriate to the model and solver
recommended_stack.parameter_guidance: Specify units, masses, rest geometry, compliance, damping formulation, fixed simulation step, substep count, solver iterations and collision parameters. XPBD uses compliance scaled by the square of the solve time step and accumulated constraint multipliers within the solve. Follow the selected implementation for multiplier initialization and damping. Improved stiffness control does not remove finite-iteration error or guarantee accuracy, stability, collision robustness or cross-backend reproducibility.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Keep simulation and rendering separate. Advance from a known initial state with fixed simulation steps and a defined deterministic constraint order where supported. For video, bake geometry or positions and any needed normals, or use checkpoints with deterministic replay. Resolve each composition timestamp from the cache or replay; never advance mutable physics once per render callback or use wall-clock delta. Test repeated, out-of-order and backward frame requests for identical states. Let Three.js render the evaluated state, and GSAP or the selected timeline control authored scene events without competing with solver-owned positions. Use HyperFrames as primary composition framework and Remotion only under its existing fallback condition. Preserve approved materials and palette tokens.
recommended_stack.limitations: Basic elastic-body XPBD does not automatically provide fluid merging, splitting, viscosity, plasticity, tearing, rigid-body contact or origami crease behavior. Such effects require appropriate additional formulations, topology handling and validation. Use authored motion instead when physical simulation adds no value.
recommended_stack.style_application: Use for optional physics-assisted elastic compression, extension, rebound and settling. Choose suitable shape or volume constraints to retain silhouette and apparent volume. Author anticipation, poses, contact timing and readable holds separately; a solver does not replace animation direction.

recommended_stack.name: Matter.js
recommended_stack.runtime: browser or Node.js for simulation baking
recommended_stack.purpose: Simulate 2D rigid bodies with gravity, collisions, restitution, friction and constraints; render their poses with the chosen visual layer.
recommended_stack.style_application: Supply collision contacts and rigid-body trajectories, then add authored area-preserving squash and stretch around impact. Matter.js does not provide true soft-body deformation.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: For video, precompute poses with seeded initial conditions and fixed Engine.update steps, then sample cached states by composition time for direct and backward seeking. Do not drive exports with Runner.run or a wall-clock loop. For interactive pages, a live runner is appropriate. This is 2D rigid-body physics, not 3D, fluid or true soft-body simulation; authored deformation remains a separate layer. Bodies.fromVertices may need poly-decomp for concave shapes. Keep critical text and imagery readable.

tech.implementation:
Background #F4EDDF and floor line #32444A. Two contrasting bodies, a #66978E ball and a #C78461 jelly block, each in nested <g> elements: an outer group for translation and an inner group for squash with transform-origin at the contact point. Key poses: anticipation (sy 0.85) → fall with stretch along velocity (sy 1.25) → impact (sx 1.3, sy 1/1.3, so area is preserved) → rebound → short hold → settle. Timing differs per object, and only one object deforms at a time. GSAP keyframes on the paused timeline; volume is checked by asserting sx·sy≈1 at sampled seeks. 3s preview: ball cycle 0–1.6s, block hop 1.4–2.6s, hold. Optional MorphSVGPlugin for contact-flattened silhouettes between compatible paths. Soft-body/glass recipe for full video: Three.js with MeshPhysicalMaterial on a deformed mesh, with XPBD fixed-step states baked and seeked from cache, labeled an approximation.
Optional recipe soft_body_glass: Use contact-aware deformation and apparent volume conservation with damped settling, not global scale pulsing. Combine Liquid Glass 069 when clear transmission is requested. XPBD is already in the technology pool: initialize once, cache/bake fixed-step states and support direct/backward seeking. Keep optical contours aligned with the deformed surface. Label analytic shape-key previews as soft-body approximations, not measured physical simulation.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: This is a motion principle, so a clean, inspectable 2D renderer with explicit pivots shows it most faithfully in 3 seconds. Uniform spring presets are rejected. XPBD and 3D glass add value only for the gummy recipe and need baking, so they stay conditional rather than inflating the preview.

motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider a hovering orb that drops on activation, compresses at contact, and triggers outward surface growth. Select only when that transformation serves the topic and assets support it; do not use this ID for ambient floating or parallax.

Consider bounded pupil following with optional delayed brows, slight head tilt, and scheduled blinks. Require suitable facial layers or a rig, preserve expression and drawing cadence, and do not interpret this as viewer eye tracking.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read the actual illustration and complete pattern description, motion_sequence and video_adaptation. Identify which scene elements implement that action. Reject unsupported geometry, absent subjects, unintended depth, broken contact points or unrelated interactions. Select none when no candidate fits; use restrained style-native motion instead. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

source_frame_review.sampling_limitation: One frame at each available second 01–08. No continuous motion, sub-second timing, audio or later scenes verified. Color families are visual observations; whole-frame measured dominant colors are not semantic background tokens.
source_frame_review.guidance: Choose scene-dependent backgrounds and readable coordinated colors. Separate material colors, source demonstration choices and surrounding UI/letterboxing. Existing swatches are examples, not permanent canvas restrictions. Keep explicit user-approved colors and medium-defining constraints. Only sampled seconds, not continuous motion or audio, were visually reviewed.

sources.style_evidence: At 1s the ball is flattened at ground contact, with impact sparks, a dotted bounce arc and a contact ellipse.
sources.palette_lesson: This author swaps whole backgrounds per chapter: near-black for physics and for the 3D chapter, saturated red-orange for transitions and type, off-white, acid chartreuse, then cobalt blue. A small shared accent set (red-orange, lime/chartreuse, cobalt, white, black) recurs across chapters, and each accent shows up as a background in one chapter and as an accent in others. These exact hues are this author's examples. What carries over is the method: flat, highly saturated digital fields with a mild radial vignette, one dominant field per section, 1–3 accents drawn from the shared set, and HUD ink that flips between dark and light (or drops to a tonal low-contrast version during transitions) to stay readable. For a new subject, build a 4–6 color set from that subject's own color world. Keep one dark neutral and one light neutral for chapters that need quiet staging, and recheck HUD and caption contrast on every field.

sources.style_evidence: Volume-preserving squash on the red figure at 7s and recovery at 8s. Vertical stretch on the blue figure at 2s and 5–7s. Bounces go from the trampoline into the air.
sources.palette_lesson: The creator chose a pastel pink-lilac room with white dots and a pink tile floor as their example environment. It isn't a medium constraint. What defines the look is the contrast: a few highly saturated, glossy, translucent jelly bodies (red, blue) set against a desaturated, high-value matte set, so each body's color glow pools on the floor and reads clearly. Props carry secondary saturated accents (yellow duck, purple ball), and the UI uses a full rainbow of glossy swatches. To reuse the style, keep the environment one or two values lighter and much less saturated than the jelly actors, give each actor a distinct hue with a matching floor glow, and keep the set pattern low-contrast so silhouettes stay readable. The source's dominant composite color sample is pink-lilac, but that comes from the downscaled whole frame and isn't a design token.

palette.composition_guidance: Use one dominant background and a clear foreground hierarchy. Keep accents subordinate except where the style calls for bold geometric fields. Preserve exact anchors; improve balance through area, spacing and placement rather than hue substitution. Gradient samples and material lighting are not extra base-color licenses.

Use chroma-js for validation, equivalent normalization and contrast assessment; evaluate gradients only when enabled and appropriate. audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of Squash and Stretch, suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.
audio_direction.integration_guidance: Select or create authorized audio assets separately from visual construction and motion design. Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

suggested_combinations.selection_guidance: Use Squash and Stretch alone when one hero object or logo needs a single expressive moment; choose a hybrid when the deformation needs a defined drawing language for characters or has to carry typographic messaging.

supporting_styles.role: Character and prop drawing: simple closed vector silhouettes that make volume-preserving deformation easy to read.

suggestions.rationale: Flat vector shapes give squash poses clean pivots and silhouettes, while the primary keeps control of timing, anticipation and settle.
suggestions.best_for: Mascot-led product explainers and short onboarding loops with a few key actions.
suggestions.video_application: Draw characters as flat SVG groups in #F4EDDF/#32444A with #66978E and #C78461 accents, then key anticipation, impact and rebound per object with explicit pivots on a GSAP timeline.
suggestions.html_application: Play one squash cycle on button press or keyboard focus by seeking the same timeline; with prefers-reduced-motion, jump straight to the settled pose.
consistency_rules: Use only the primary's four palette tokens, not flat-vector default brights.
Deformation preserves apparent area and pivots at contact points.
Only the acting object deforms; background shapes stay rigid.
avoid: Uniform spring presets on every element.
Gradients or detailed shading that hide the silhouette change.

supporting_styles.role: Typography: headline words that land with anticipation, compress on impact and settle into a readable hold.

suggestions.rationale: Kinetic type gives the bounce a message, and the squash discipline keeps letter motion weighted instead of jittery.
suggestions.best_for: Title cards, feature callouts and social intros where one or two words need physical emphasis.
suggestions.video_application: Animate word groups (not single glyphs) with scale-Y compression at the baseline pivot, one key word at a time, and hold each settled word for at least a beat before the next one enters.
suggestions.html_application: Hero heading entrance driven by scroll or load on a seekable timeline, with real DOM text for screen readers and a static fallback when motion is reduced.
consistency_rules: Text in #32444A on #F4EDDF; accents mark emphasis words only.
Deform from baseline pivots and return to exact glyph proportions at rest.
One emphasis word bounces per phrase.
avoid: Stretching body copy or small text past legibility.
Continuous wobble after the word has settled.

productionPolicy.principle: Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique.
productionPolicy.style_renderer: Owns visual construction: drawing, geometry, materials, lighting, typography, masks, textures, and specialist asset generation. Use the style-specific recommended technologies and implementation guidance.
productionPolicy.motion_engine: Owns trajectories, transforms, easing, transitions, deformation, and simulation. Select engines or algorithms appropriate to the action, with one owner for each animated property.
productionPolicy.render_pipeline: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.
productionPolicy.integration: Visual and motion layers expose deterministic state at composition time, or supply baked assets or frame sequences. The pipeline supplies seekable time and composes their output. Timeline registration and frame hooks are integration adapters, not substitutes for style-specific rendering or motion.
productionPolicy.selection: Choose only needed stack entries. A technology may serve multiple roles, but document its actual responsibility. Optional authoring, interaction, color, and preprocessing tools are not mandatory renderers or motion engines.

motionReferences.name: Immersive Float
motionReferences.description: An orb hovers above a soft form. Activation makes the orb fall and compress on contact; a growth front then spreads across the receiving surface from the impact point. Small sparks and flowers accompany the expanding front. The central action is a triggered drop, impact, and spreading transformation, rather than unrelated layers drifting.
motion_sequence: Establish the hovering orb, the receiving soft form, and their separation.
On click or equivalent activation, drop the orb and show a squash at contact.
Begin surface growth at the impact point and expand it across the form, with small sparks and flowers following the growth boundary.
Hold the transformed surface so the result of the action remains readable.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Author a trigger time, then time the descent, impact compression, and surface-growth reveal relative to it. Evaluate every stage directly from composition time or a baked cache. Keep growth absent before contact and restore the correct pre-impact state on backward seeks.

suggested_libraries.purpose: Render genuine 3D forms or shader treatments when a 2D solution is insufficient.

suggested_libraries.name: PixiJS

suggested_libraries.name: Motion

suggested_libraries.runtime: browser; motion/react for mounted React components
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. tech.implementation: Use a modeled orb and receiving surface for true 3D, or authored layers for an explicitly flat adaptation. Animate descent and contact compression before driving a surface-space growth mask from the impact origin. Use prepared textures, geometry, or sprites for the growth material and small boundary accents. Parameterize the mask and accent placement deterministically; these are suggested implementation methods, not verified production tools or a physical simulation.

Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motionReferences.name: Cursor-Driven Gaze Tracking
motionReferences.description: A character follows a pointer with pupil motion constrained to its eye sockets. Brows can follow with a short delay, the head can tilt subtly, and periodic blinks add secondary expression. Eye direction remains coordinated; this is illustrated character animation, not measurement of the viewer's gaze.

Move the target and shift the pupils within their sockets; add delayed brow movement and a slight head tilt when the assets support them.
Include scheduled blinks and hold readable reactions, returning to a neutral pose when the designed interaction ends.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Author the target path and any visible cursor on the composition timeline. Evaluate gaze directly from target position at each time. Model any delay analytically from the authored path or bake it; do not rely on a live smoothing loop or webcam input.

motionReferences.name: Scroll-Driven Chaptered Scene Transition
motionReferences.description: Scroll progress coordinates a handoff between narrative chapters. An outgoing scene yields to an incoming scene through a chosen fade, wipe, panel rotation, or shared-element move; text and media states change with the same progress. Clear start and end states preserve reading order in both scroll directions.
motion_sequence: Establish the outgoing chapter and a readable closing state.
Across a defined progress window, coordinate outgoing and incoming scene states with one selected transition treatment and synchronized copy.
Resolve the incoming chapter into its readable state before beginning the next handoff; reversing progress retraces the same transition.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Schedule chapter windows and transition intervals on composition time. Explicitly choose the handoff type. If the style requires a continuous shot, use a coherent camera or spatial handoff instead of an incompatible cut.
